target_customer: Health plans, state agencies, IPAs and MSOs, especially Medi-Cal managed care plans
problem: Healthcare organizations spend heavy consulting and staff time tracking regulatory changes, mapping them to policies and preparing audits.
business_model: enterprise SaaS for compliance and regulatory change management

founders.name: Edward Tiong
previous_startups: Two earlier startups (YC page says third-time founder; names and outcomes not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he holds 2 patents.

investors: California Health Care Foundation Innovation Fund

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM retrieval and mapping of regulations to policies is standard AI engineering, but accuracy, audit trails and healthcare security (SOC 2, HIPAA) add hard requirements.

defensibility.rationale: Policy libraries, audit evidence and certifications embed the product in plan operations, though general compliance vendors could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition or copy was documented in sources found.

market_need_then: Medicaid managed care plans face frequent state and federal guidance letters and audits; the CHCF reports one plan cut compliance spend from 2 million to 120 thousand a year, which is a vendor-era claim.

branding.domain_note: Company site is readily.ai; one vendor directory lists readily.co, so the history is unclear.

identity.voice_and_tone: Trust and control focused: 'Close compliance gaps as regulations change', stressing confidentiality, assurance and human review.

brand_strength.rationale: Enterprise buyers care about references and certifications more than brand, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Readily joined YC in Summer 2023 and focused on California Medicaid managed care plans, reporting 15 plans including L.A. Care and 25 million covered lives across 46 states by 2026. It raised an 11 million Series A in October 2026 led by Define Ventures to expand into operational oversight. Traction with regulated buyers and a clear compliance pain explain the raise, with no layoffs or exit reported.
notes: Series A cross-checked across HIT Consultant, Fierce Healthcare, MobiHealthNews and Wilson Sonsini via search results (the Fierce page itself returned 403 when fetched); one outlet dates it 2026-10-14. A 125K seed from Dealroom and an SUTD Venture investment from CB Insights are single-source and unverified. Competitor list left empty because the search returned 2026 vendor comparison pages and no 2023 sources. YC lists founding as 2024 while CB Insights says 2023.
